title: Add export checksum and anomaly flagging to detect proration drift
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several customer investigations in Q4 and ongoing reconciliations indicate small, silent proration drift in the nightly Stripe/NetSuite billing export pipeline. These drifts are often under the alerting threshold and only show up as invoice differences during manual audits. This ticket implements an auditing layer: deterministic checksums and anomaly flagging at each export stage to detect silent offset drift and stop bad exports before they reach accounting systems.

Problem details: The export pipeline has multiple stages (hourly usage rollups -> proration merger -> invoice line generation -> Stripe/NetSuite payload builder). Multiple failure modes can silently alter totals: eventual-consistency reorders from delayed webhooks, racey invoice-line merges that drop fractional cents, and non-deterministic map iteration in an older aggregation job. These cause subtle mismatches between the canonical usage ledger and the final export (e.g., -$0.25 to +$1.10 per invoice) which are hard to trace after export.

Root cause hypothesis: We observed cases where the aggregation step and the invoice-line merge operate on slightly different input sets due to late-arriving usage, and there is no end-to-end invariant check between the canonical ledger and exported totals. The export writes only final line items; there is no cryptographic or checksum metadata attached at intermediate stages.

Proposed solution: 1) Add deterministic, stage-stable checksums to every export artifact (hourly-usage bundle, proration diff, invoice-line bundle) computed using a stable canonicalization method (sorted keys, normalized currency rounding, UTF-8 stable serialization) and a fast checksum (CRC32 or xxhash64). 2) Persist checksum and a small export manifest (counts, sum_in_cents, currency, exported_ids) alongside artifacts in export storage. 3) Produce an end-to-end reconciliation check that verifies manifest.sum_in_cents equals the canonical ledger's sum within configured tolerance and checksum equality for the canonicalized payload. 4) If mismatch > tolerance or checksum mismatch, mark the export as FAILED, raise PagerDuty, write a blocking marker to prevent downstream pushing to Stripe/NetSuite, and create a reconciliation ticket with links to artifacts. 5) Add anomaly metrics and dashboards: export_checksum_mismatch_count, export_sum_delta_cents, export_blocked_count; retention for 90 days.

Design constraints and trade-offs: - Checksums must be computed deterministically and cheaply; we avoid heavyweight crypto HMACs to keep cost low, but will include optional signing in a follow-up if adversarial tampering is a concern. - Must not change existing exported payload schema (so Stripe/NetSuite consumers unaffected). The manifest will be stored alongside artifacts in S3 and referenced by the export job. - Tolerance should be configurable per-customer (default 100 cents or 0.5% whichever is greater) to avoid blocking noisy small customers.

Acceptance criteria: - New export pipeline emits manifest files for 100% of exports in staging and prod canary. - When we intentionally inject a single-cent discrepancy in test data, the system flags the export and prevents a downstream push. - Dashboards surface checksum_mismatch_count with drilldowns to manifest S3 keys. - Runbook documented for investigation/playbook and one retrospective after first blocked export. - Integration tests cover canonicalization changes and checksum computation.

Rollout plan: 1) Implement manifest writer and checksum logic in export-worker (feature-flagged). 2) Enable read-only sanity checks in prod for 2 weeks (no blocking) while we observe metrics. 3) Enable blocking behavior in a single region and particular tenant cohort (canary customers) for 1 week. 4) Gradual ramp to all exports. 5) Post-rollout: run a full backfill check for past 30 days and create remediation tickets for any mismatches.

Operational notes: - Alerts should page on high-severity mismatches (>= $10 or >1% of invoice) and write to an internal Slack channel for lower severity. - Add a lightweight endpoint to query a manifest by export_id and present sums/checksums for manual review (console integration later).

Security and privacy: Manifests contain only export metadata and aggregated sums and exported IDs; no raw customer PII or usage text will be included. If additional signing is needed, follow-up will go through security review.

Related: This is complementary to the existing late-webhook and proration fixes but focuses on detection and automated blocking so human auditors can remediate before invoices are sent.
comments: 2026-01-12 Aisha Patel: Triage notes - several customer tickets (CS-4532, CS-4591) traced to small invoice deltas. Decided to prioritize detection+blocking before attempting full auto-fix. Created design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/Export+Manifest+Design

2026-01-18 Liam Chen: Investigation - replayed 90 days of exports in staging and found 18 exports with >20 cents delta due to non-deterministic map order in legacy aggregator. POC checksum generator implemented in staging branch. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/3412

2026-01-25 QA (Nina Gomez): POC results - checksum calculation stable across JVM restarts and library upgrades. Found one false-positive due to rounding difference in an old Python consumer; added canonical rounding rule to design doc.

2026-02-05 Dev (Liam Chen): Feature-flagged manifest writer merged to main with unit + integration tests. End-to-end test harness updated to validate manifest roundtrip. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/3479

2026-02-22 Ops (Marcus Lee): Deployed read-only checks to canary region; observed 7 mismatches in first week. Created incident notes and opened ENG-61842 as follow-up for the aggregator bug we surfaced.

2026-03-10 Liam Chen: Preparing rollout - blocking behavior gated by tenant-label 'billing-checks-enabled'. Plan to enable blocking for 10 canary tenants on 2026-03-15. Asking SRE to add PagerDuty escalation if blocked export sum delta >= 1000 cents.
